newsitem.title: FRANCE: Iraq enters grain market for more French wheat.
newsitem.headline: Iraq enters grain market for more French wheat.

text.p: Iraq, which bought French wheat under its Union Nations oil-for-food deal last month, is back in the grain market for 100,000 tonnes of French wheat in March and April, traders said on Wednesday.
The deadline for offers in its latest tender for wheat is January 14, they said.
Grain traders said last month that Iraq had bought 300,000 tonnes of French wheat for January and February using money raised from oil sales under a humanitarian pact with the U.N.
But traders said the new purchase tender raised further doubts over whether the full 300,000 tonnes had been finalised.
A French budget ministry official told Reuters on Tuesday that France was seeking U.N. approval for recent wheat sales to Iraq of 200,000 tonnes instead of 300,000 tonnes.
Iraq's deal with the U.N. allows it to sell crude worth $2 billion over six months to pay for foreign food and medicine.
